questions.question: Which crop became a foundation of many Mesoamerican societies?
choices: Wheat
Maize
Barley
Potatoes only

questions.question: Which civilization built its capital, Tenochtitlan, on an island in Lake Texcoco?
choices: The Inca
The Olmec
The Mexica, often called the Aztec
The Moche

questions.question: What were chinampas?
choices: Inca record-keeping cords
Maya stone calendars
Andean mountain roads
Raised agricultural plots built in shallow lake areas

questions.question: Which civilization created a large empire centered in the Andes with its capital at Cusco?
choices: The Inca
The Maya
The Olmec
The Mexica

questions.question: Why did the Inca build extensive roads across the Andes?
choices: To prevent all trade between settlements
To connect regions and support communication, administration, and movement
To replace agriculture with mining
To mark the edge of the Sahara

questions.question: What were quipu used for in the Inca Empire?
choices: Growing maize in lake gardens
Building stone arches
Recording information with knotted cords
Tracking European ships

questions.question: Which civilization is known for early monumental sculpture and influence in the Gulf Coast region of Mesoamerica?
choices: The Inca
The Songhai
The Hittite
The Olmec

questions.question: Why did Maya city-states develop systems of writing and calendars?
choices: They supported record keeping, ritual, political life, and tracking time
They replaced all local languages
They were used only to navigate the Atlantic
They ended the need for trade

questions.question: A farming community in the Andes builds terraces on a steep slope. What is the main agricultural purpose?
choices: To make the mountain taller
To create level planting areas and manage soil and water on hillsides
To prevent all rainfall from reaching crops
To connect the Andes to the Nile

questions.question: How did the geography of the Andes influence Inca society?
choices: The mountains made agriculture impossible everywhere
The Andes prevented any centralized government
Mountain terrain shaped farming, transportation, and regional connections
The empire existed only on flat coastal plains

questions.question: What does the term Mesoamerica refer to?
choices: The entire South American continent
A medieval European kingdom
A river valley in eastern Africa
A cultural region of present-day Mexico and Central America

questions.question: Why was trade important among Mesoamerican societies?
choices: It moved goods such as obsidian, cacao, textiles, and ideas across regions
It made local resources unnecessary
It prevented political alliances
It occurred only after Spanish conquest

questions.question: A historian compares Spanish accounts with Indigenous sources about the conquest of the Mexica Empire. Why use both?
choices: Spanish accounts always contain every viewpoint
Different sources can reveal perspective, bias, and experiences omitted by one account
Indigenous sources cannot provide historical evidence
Comparing accounts eliminates the need for context

questions.question: Which statement about the Maya is accurate?
choices: The Maya formed a single empire that controlled all of South America
Maya civilization began after the Spanish conquest
Maya peoples built city-states and developed writing, mathematics, and astronomy
The Maya had no agricultural systems

questions.question: What challenge did the Inca face in governing a large empire across varied terrain?
choices: Maintaining contact across a single small island
Managing a navy on the Mediterranean Sea
Growing rice in the Nile Delta
Communicating and transporting people and goods across long distances and mountains

questions.question: Why were potatoes and other high-altitude crops important in the Andes?
choices: They were adapted to local environments and supported food supplies
They could grow only in tropical rainforests
They replaced all trade
They were first introduced from Europe before the Inca

questions.question: Which feature helped the Mexica expand their power in the Valley of Mexico?
choices: A network of transatlantic steamships
Military alliances and control of tribute from subject communities
The construction of the Great Wall
Control of the Sahara's caravan routes

questions.question: A city grows on a lake island and uses raised fields to increase food production. Which example best fits this description?
choices: Cusco and quipu
Machu Picchu and Roman aqueducts
Tenochtitlan and chinampas
Chichen Itza and Nile irrigation

questions.question: Why should the terms 'Aztec' and 'Mexica' be used carefully in historical writing?
choices: They describe the Inca Empire
They are names for the Maya writing system
They were created by the Olmec
They can refer to related but not identical political or cultural groupings

questions.question: What is one lasting effect of Spanish conquest on Indigenous communities in the Americas?
choices: Population loss, political change, and cultural transformation, alongside continued Indigenous survival and adaptation
The disappearance of all Indigenous languages and traditions
No changes to land ownership or government
The end of all cultural exchange
